blocks.text: I can form the letters i, l and t.
Your hands and wrists get stronger when you exercise them.
Warming up will help to improve your handwriting. It will help you to hold your pencil in the tripod grip for longer.

items.title: Finger tap warm-up
items.sub: Pretend you have Play-Doh on your thumb. Squeeze it with each finger in turn.

items.title: Rolling wrists warm-up
items.sub: Pretend to stir with a wooden spoon, one way and then the other way.

blocks.text: Practising writing patterns helps to prepare us for writing letters.

items.title: Up and down
items.sub: Helps with letters that go up and down.

items.title: Zig-zag
items.sub: Helps with letters that have straight or zig-zag lines.

items.title: Up, round and down
items.sub: Helps with letters that have loops or curves.

blocks.text: Copy and continue the pattern with your tripod grip. Do not lift your pencil.

items.def: Lines used to help people write neatly. They keep letters the same size and straight.

blocks.text: Tramlines have four lines. Each line has a name. From the top down:

items: The top line is the **ascender line**.
The next line down is the **x-height line**.
The next line down is the **baseline**.
The very bottom line is the **descender line**.

blocks.q: Match each tramline to its name.

blocks.text: Let’s look closely at the letter i. What can you see?

items: The letter i is a small letter.
The letter i is an x-height letter.
The letter i has a dot at the top.
The letter i starts at the top and finishes with a flick.

items.def: Letters that reach the middle height on the line.
Regular-sized letters that are not as tall as the tall letters.

blocks.text: Sit comfortably and hold your pencil. Then:

items: 1. Start on the x-height line.
2. Go down to the baseline and do a flick.
3. Take your pencil off the page.
4. Add a dot at the top.

blocks.q: Which of these is true about the letter i?
options: It has a dot at the top
blocks.why: The letter i is a small letter. It starts at the top and has a dot at the top.

blocks.q: Which line do you start on to write i?
blocks.why: To write i, start on the x-height line, go down to the baseline, flick, then add a dot.

items: The letter l is a tall letter.
The letter l goes down and finishes with a flick.
Part of the letter l goes above the x-height line.

items.def: Letters that reach up high and are usually taller than the other letters in the alphabet.
The part of a letter that extends above the level of the top of an x. It goes above the x-height line.

blocks.text: The letter l is an example of a letter with an ascender.

items: 1. Start on the ascender line, because l is a tall letter.
2. Go all the way down to the baseline. Do not take your pencil off the paper.
3. When you reach the baseline, add a flick.

blocks.q: Which line do you start on to write l?
blocks.why: The letter l is a tall letter, so you start on the ascender line and go down to the baseline.

blocks.q: What do we call the part of a letter that goes above the x-height line?
blocks.why: An ascender is the part of a letter that goes above the x-height line. The letter l has one.

items: The letter t goes down and finishes with a flick.
The letter t has a cross on the x-height line.
1. Start just above the x-height line.
2. Go down and finish with a flick.
3. Take your pencil off the page.
4. Add a cross on the x-height line.

blocks.q: Where does the cross of the letter t go?
blocks.why: The letter t has a cross on the x-height line.

blocks.q: What do you do before you add the cross to t?
options: Take your pencil off the page
Stay on the page and draw a dot
blocks.why: You lift your pencil off the page to add the cross.

items.def: Groups of letters that look similar and belong to the same group.

blocks.text: The letters i, l and t are formed in similar ways. They all start at the top and finish with a flick. So they are in the same letter family.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Letter families are not letters that are next to each other in the alphabet. Letters are in a family when they are formed in a similar way.

blocks.q: Match each letter to something you do when you write it.

pairs.b: Add a dot at the top
Add a cross on the x-height line

blocks.q: How are letters put into letter families?
options: They are formed in similar ways
They are next to each other in the alphabet
blocks.why: Letters that are formed in a similar way are in the same letter family.

items: The letters i, l and t are in a letter family. They all go down and finish with a flick.
The letter i has a dot at the top.
The letter l has an ascender: part of it goes above the x-height line.
The letter t has a cross on the x-height line.

flashcards.front: Why do we warm up our hands before writing?
flashcards.back: Our hands and wrists get stronger when we exercise them. It helps our handwriting and helps us hold the pencil in the tripod grip for longer.

flashcards.front: What helps to prepare us for writing letters?

flashcards.back: Lines used to help people write neatly. They keep letters the same size and straight.

flashcards.front: Name the four tramlines from the top down.
flashcards.back: Ascender line, x-height line, baseline, descender line.

flashcards.front: Which line do you start on to write the letter i?
What do you add to the letter i after the flick?
flashcards.back: A dot at the top. Take your pencil off the page first.

flashcards.front: What sort of letter is i?
flashcards.back: A small letter and an x-height letter.

flashcards.front: Which line do you start on to write the letter l?
flashcards.back: The ascender line, because l is a tall letter.

The part of a letter that goes above the x-height line.

The letter l has an ascender.

flashcards.front: How is the letter l formed?
flashcards.back: It goes down and finishes with a flick.

flashcards.front: What does the letter t have on the x-height line?

flashcards.back:
Groups of letters that are formed in a similar way.

i, l and t all start at the top and finish with a flick.
